findings.title: Only Flux extractor shipped; SD3-5/SD3/Pixart code (incl. SOTA rows) absent
findings.quote: We evaluate our strategies on four different pre-trained DiTs
findings.claim: The paper reports DiTF results for Pixart-alpha, SD3, SD3-5 and Flux (Tables 2, 3, 5, 7), but the repo's src/ contains only the Flux model (src/flux/**); eval_spair.py hard-restricts --dift_model to 'flux' (choices=['flux'], and raises otherwise at lines 100-103), and there is no SD3/SD3-5/Pixart feature-extraction code anywhere.
findings.concern: None of the DiTFsd3-5 / DiTFsd3 / DiTFpixart numbers can be reproduced, including the headline SOTA row DiTFsd3-5(ours)† (SPair 72.2, AP-10K-I.S. 71.3); the 'new state-of-the-art for DiTs' claim rests mostly on models with no released code.
findings.resolution: Release the feature-extraction code (the analogue of feat_flux.py/forward_feat) for SD3, SD3-5 and Pixart-alpha, plus the eval driver that consumes them.
findings.reason: Confirmed: eval_spair.py line 314 restricts --dift_model choices=['flux'] and raises at lines 100-103; src/ contains only src/flux/; no SD3/SD3-5/Pixart code found anywhere in repo.

findings.title: DINOv2-integrated (†) pipeline entirely absent — no DINO load, concat, or PCA
findings.quote: We extracted DINOv2 features from the token facet of the 11th layer of the model.
findings.claim: The '†: Integrating DINOv2 features' rows of Tables 2-3 (which include the best-reported results, e.g. DiTFsd3-5† = 72.2 on SPair) require loading DINOv2, concatenating it channel-wise with DiT features, and the pair-PCA of Eq. (14); none of this exists in the repo. The only PCA helper, eval_spair.py:pca_feature_pair (line 32), is never called (grep: sole occurrence is its def).
findings.concern: Every '†' number in the paper — including the overall SOTA claims — is unreproducible; the leftover pca_feature_pair function is dead code and no DINOv2 model is ever instantiated.
findings.resolution: Release the DINOv2 loading + channel concatenation + pair-PCA integration code, and wire pca_feature_pair (or its replacement) into the eval path.
findings.paper_ref: Appendix C (Integration of DINOv2 feature), Eq. (14); Tables 2, 3 († rows)
findings.reason: Confirmed: pca_feature_pair defined at line 32 is its sole occurrence (never called); no DINOv2 loading or channel-concat code exists anywhere in repo; paper quote located in paper_text.txt.

findings.title: AP-10K and PF-Pascal evaluation code absent (only SPair-71k implemented)
findings.quote: we conduct experiments on three popular benchmarks: SPair-71k
findings.claim: The paper evaluates on SPair-71k, PF-Pascal and AP-10K (I.S./C.S./C.F.), but the repo ships only eval_spair.py, which is hardwired to SPair's PairAnnotation/test JSON layout (eval_spair.py:72-98). Grep for 'ap10k|pf.?author' across *.py/*.sh returns nothing.
findings.concern: The abstract's second headline claim ('+4.4% on AP-10K-C.S.', text: 64.6 -> 69.4 on C.S.) and all PF-Pascal numbers (Table 3) have no code and cannot be reproduced.
findings.resolution: Release the AP-10K and PF-Pascal evaluation drivers (data loading, split selection, and PCK-per-image computation for the I.S./C.S./C.F. settings).
findings.reason: Confirmed: eval_spair.py lines 72-98 hardwire 'PairAnnotation/test' SPair layout; grep for ap10k/pf.?author across repo returns nothing.

findings.title: Channel-discard strategy (a named contribution) is not implemented anywhere
findings.quote: we zero out the corresponding dimensions of these weakly massive activations in the post-AdaLN features
findings.claim: The paper's channel-discard strategy zeroes specific post-AdaLN dimensions (for Flux the massive-activation dims 154 and 1446). eval_spair.py applies only the AdaLN modulation (line 190: `src_ft = (1 + src_scale) * src_ft + src_shift`) and never zeroes any channel; grep for 'discard', '154', '1446', '676', 'zero' over *.py returns no zeroing code.
findings.concern: One of the paper's four itemized contributions and the top row of the ablation (Table 4: +AdaLN 65.3 -> +Channel discard 67.1 on SPair) cannot be reproduced or even located in the code.
findings.resolution: Release the channel-discard implementation and the mechanism that identifies which post-AdaLN dimensions are zeroed per model.
findings.reason: Confirmed: eval_spair.py line 190 applies only AdaLN modulation; grep for 'discard','154','1446','676' in all .py files returns nothing; no channel zeroing code anywhere.

findings.title: No toggles/scripts for Table 4 (Original/+AdaLN) or Table 5 (condition) ablations
findings.quote: We report the PCK per point for SPair-71k and PCK per image for
findings.claim: eval_spair.py always applies AdaLN modulation (line 190) and always conditions on both t and c (feat_flux.py builds prompt embeds and passes a fixed timestep); there is no flag to produce the 'Original' (no-AdaLN) row, and no way to vary the condition among {original, c, t, t&c} for Table 5.
findings.concern: The ablations that establish the method's core mechanism (Tables 4 and 5) are not runnable from the released code without editing it, so their numbers are unverifiable.
findings.resolution: Add command-line switches (or scripts) that reproduce each ablation row: no-AdaLN, +AdaLN, +channel-discard, and the condition sweep original/c/t/t&c.
findings.reason: Confirmed: eval_spair.py line 190 always applies AdaLN; feat_flux.py line 197 has .mean(0) commented out; no flag to disable AdaLN or vary conditioning type.

findings.title: Segmentation (ADE20K), geometric (HPatches) and temporal (DAVIS) code absent
findings.quote: we conduct semantic segmentation experiments on
findings.claim: Table 6 (ADE20K semantic segmentation, incl. training a segmentation head), Table 8 (HPatches homography via cv2.findHomography), and Table 9 (DAVIS-2017 video segmentation) are all reported, but no code for any of these tasks exists in the repo (grep 'ade20k|hpatches|davis' over *.py/*.sh returns nothing).
findings.concern: The generalization evidence in Section 5.4 and Appendices D-E cannot be reproduced from the released code.
findings.resolution: Release the ADE20K segmentation training/eval, the HPatches homography pipeline, and the DAVIS label-propagation pipeline.
findings.reason: Confirmed: grep for ade20k/hpatches/davis across all repo files returns nothing; only eval_spair.py and test_spair.sh exist as eval scripts.

findings.title: No dependency spec and no README/results table for the DiTF eval pipeline
findings.quote:
import cv2
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import gc
import copy
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
from torchvision import transforms as T
from math import sqrt
import seaborn as sns
findings.claim: eval_spair.py / feat_flux.py require diffusers, opencv (cv2), scikit-learn, scipy, seaborn, matplotlib, tqdm, einops, but the repo root has no requirements.txt / pyproject.toml / setup.py / environment.yml and no README (only eval_spair.py, test_spair.sh, model_cards/, model_licenses/, src/). The sole dependency list is src/flux.egg-info/requires.txt, which is the upstream flux package's manifest and lists none of diffusers/cv2/sklearn/scipy/seaborn.
findings.concern: The environment cannot be rebuilt from the repo, and there is no README with the exact reproduction commands or a results table, so even the one implemented experiment is not turn-key.
findings.resolution: Add a pinned requirements/environment file covering all imports and a README documenting data layout, weights, and the exact command + expected numbers.
findings.paper_ref: Checklist Q5 ('Datasets and codes are available ... to faithfully reproduce')
findings.reason: Confirmed: eval_spair.py lines 13-20 match the quote exactly; repo root contains only eval_spair.py, test_spair.sh, model_cards/, model_licenses/, src/ — no README or dependency spec.

findings.title: No code identifies the massive-activation dimensions or produces the analysis figures
findings.quote: the SD3-5 model exhibits massive activations concentrated in a single feature dimension (676)
findings.claim: The paper's central empirical analysis — massive activations concentrated at fixed dims (SD3-5: 676; Flux: 154 and 1446), the per-dimension mean/variance of Table 1, and the pre/post-AdaLN visualizations of Figs 2-5/10-16 — has no supporting code; the specific dimensions never appear in the repo (grep '676|154|1446' finds nothing).
findings.concern: The paper's identification/characterization of massive activations (which motivates the whole method) is not reproducible from released code.
findings.resolution: Release the scripts that compute the ranked-dimension statistics (Table 1) and locate/visualize the massive-activation dimensions per model.
findings.reason: Confirmed: grep for '676','154','1446' across all repo .py files returns nothing; no dimension-analysis or visualization scripts present.

findings.title: Eval computes only PCK@0.10; the @0.01 and @0.05 columns have no code
findings.claim: The PCK threshold is hardcoded to 0.1; the script emits only PCK@0.10. Tables 3 and 8 report PCK@0.01 and @0.05 (and 1/3/5 px) as well, which this code never computes.
findings.concern: The @0.01/@0.05 entries across the paper's tables are not produced by the released code (a one-line change, but as shipped they are untraceable).
findings.resolution: Parameterize the PCK threshold (or loop over {0.01,0.05,0.10}) so the reported multi-threshold columns are reproducible.
findings.reason: Confirmed: eval_spair.py line 252 hardcodes `<= 0.1` as the single PCK threshold; no looping over other thresholds.

findings.title: Shipped test_spair.sh (ensemble_size=1) crashes: chunk(2) returns one chunk
findings.quote:
feat_pred_uncond, feat_pred_text = src_ft_raw.chunk(2)
# src_ft_raw = feat_pred_uncond + guidance_scale * (feat_pred_text - feat_pred_uncond)
src_ft_raw = feat_pred_text
findings.claim: The saved per-image feature has batch dim == ensemble_size (feat_flux.py returns unet_ft without averaging — the `.mean(0)` at feat_flux.py:197 is commented out). The released test_spair.sh passes `--ensemble_size 1`, so src_ft_raw has shape [1, 3072, 48, 48]. torch.chunk(x, 2, dim=0) on a size-1 dim returns a SINGLE chunk, so `feat_pred_uncond, feat_pred_text = src_ft_raw.chunk(2)` raises `ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 2, got 1)`. This is the first statement in the per-pair loop, so evaluation dies before any PCK is produced. Reproduced in _audit_code/check_chunk_crash.py (out/chunk_crash.json).
findings.concern: The repo's only end-to-end reproduction command crashes on the first evaluated pair, so the one implemented headline number (SPair-71k / Flux, 67.1) cannot be reproduced as shipped; the chunk(uncond/text) split is also structurally vestigial because feat_flux never produces an uncond pass.
findings.resolution: Remove the chunk/uncond-text split (feat_flux emits only the text-conditioned feature), or set ensemble_size==2; confirm which ensemble_size and feature layout produced the paper numbers.
findings.reason: Confirmed: eval_spair.py lines 175-177 match quote; feat_flux.py line 197 has .mean(0) commented out; test_spair.sh uses --ensemble_size 1; check_chunk_crash.py output confirms ValueError with ensemble_size=1.

findings.title: Paper states 960x960 input; released script uses 768x768
findings.quote: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 python eval_spair.py --dataset spair --dataset_path spair-71k_path --save_path dfm_feats/spair_flux_img768 --dift_model flux --img_size 768 768 --t 260 --ft_index 28 --ensemble_size 1
findings.claim: Appendix C states 'We set the input image size as 960x960 for DiTs'. The released reproduction script instead runs at 768x768 (and names its output dir spair_flux_img768), and the eval_spair.py CLI default is even smaller ([512,512]).
findings.concern: Correspondence PCK is resolution-sensitive; a reviewer following the shipped command will not reproduce the paper's stated 960px configuration, so the two disagree on a result-affecting setting.
findings.resolution: Clarify which resolution produced Table 2/3 (960 vs 768), and ship a script matching it.
findings.reason: Confirmed: test_spair.sh line 1 matches the quote exactly with --img_size 768 768; paper text states 960x960 for DiTs.

findings.title: Block-index/timestep grid search — split not stated; search code absent
findings.quote: we conducted grid search experiments to identify the optimal hyperparameters
findings.claim: The block index k and timestep t are per-model tuned (Table 7; Fig 12 shows SPair-71k PCK vs k and vs t). The code takes k (ft_index) and t as fixed CLI args (test_spair.sh: --ft_index 28 --t 260); the grid-search harness is not in the repo, and the paper does not state whether the k/t curves in Fig 12 are on a validation split or on the SPair-71k test set used for the headline numbers.
findings.concern: If the optimal k/t were selected on the SPair-71k test set (no validation split is described for these training-free features), the reported numbers are optimistically biased by tuning on the evaluation set.
findings.resolution: Authors: state the split used for the Fig 12 grid search and release the search harness; confirm k/t were fixed without touching the test set.
findings.paper_ref: Appendix C (Investigation on block index k and timestep t); Figure 12; Table 7
findings.reason: Confirmed: paper_text.txt line 1682 contains the quoted grid search text with no mention of a validation split; test_spair.sh has ft_index and t fixed; no grid-search harness in repo.
